disambiguation_tip: Think of a 'successful exit' from a startup: éxito means success, while salida is the physical door out.
example_es: El proyecto fue un gran éxito para todo el equipo.
example_en: The project was a great success for the whole team.

disambiguation_tip: You file papers inside a carpeta on your desk and walk on an alfombra on the floor.
example_es: Guarda los documentos importantes en la carpeta azul.
example_en: Keep the important documents in the blue folder.

disambiguation_tip: Embarazada means carrying a baby (pregnant); to say you feel embarrassed, use avergonzado or tener vergüenza.
example_es: Mi hermana está embarazada de seis meses.
example_en: My sister is six months pregnant.

disambiguation_tip: Soportar is bearing a heavy burden ('I can't stand it'); to back or help someone is apoyar.
example_es: Elena no soporta el ruido de la calle por la noche.
example_en: Elena cannot stand the noise from the street at night.

disambiguation_tip: Realizar means to make something real by doing it; realizing a fact in your mind is darse cuenta de.
example_es: Los investigadores realizaron un estudio muy completo.
example_en: The researchers carried out a very thorough study.

disambiguation_tip: Link actual and actualmente to 'at the current moment' (like French actuellement), not 'in fact'.
example_es: Actualmente vivimos en el centro de Madrid.
example_en: Currently we live in downtown Madrid.

disambiguation_tip: El presidente actual is the current president, not the 'real' one.
example_es: La situación actual requiere mucha paciencia.
example_en: The current situation requires a lot of patience.

disambiguation_tip: When you asistir a una reunión, you merely show up and attend; ayudar is to help.
example_es: Más de cien personas asistieron a la conferencia.
example_en: More than a hundred people attended the conference.

disambiguation_tip: Largo measures length (long), whereas grande measures overall size (large/big).
example_es: Fue un viaje muy largo en tren.
example_en: It was a very long trip by train.

disambiguation_tip: Ends in -ería like panadería (bakery)—a shop where you buy libros (books). Borrow books at a biblioteca.
example_es: Compré esta novela en la librería del barrio.
example_en: I bought this novel at the neighborhood bookstore.

disambiguation_tip: Connected to leer (to read) and lector (reader): lectura is the act or passage of reading.
example_es: La lectura diaria mejora el vocabulario rápidamente.
example_en: Daily reading improves vocabulary rapidly.

disambiguation_tip: Una persona sensible feels emotions deeply (sensitive); a level-headed, practical person is sensata.
example_es: Tiene la piel muy sensible al sol.
example_en: She has skin that is very sensitive to the sun.

disambiguation_tip: From Latin cor (heart): recordar is bringing something back to heart (remembering); recording audio is grabar.
example_es: No recuerdo el nombre de aquella calle.
example_en: I do not remember the name of that street.

disambiguation_tip: Cousin of English 'delinquent' and 'delict': un delito is a legal offense or crime.
example_es: El juez declaró que aquello era un delito grave.
example_en: The judge declared that it was a serious crime.

disambiguation_tip: Think of 'what succeeded/followed in time': un suceso is simply an event (or news incident), while éxito is success.
example_es: El periódico publicó todos los detalles del suceso.
example_en: The newspaper published all the details of the event.

disambiguation_tip: Pretender is serious ambition (what you aim or intend to do); faking or pretending is fingir.
example_es: El autor pretende explicar la historia con claridad.
example_en: The author intends to explain the history clearly.

disambiguation_tip: Estar constipado refers to nasal congestion from a head cold, not digestive trouble.
example_es: Estoy un poco constipado por el cambio de clima.
example_en: I have a bit of a cold from the change in weather.

disambiguation_tip: Where things are 'fabricated' (manufactured): fábrica is a factory, while cloth fabric is tela.
example_es: La fábrica produce automóviles eléctricos.
example_en: The factory produces electric cars.

disambiguation_tip: Parientes are extended family relatives; only your mother and father are tus padres.
example_es: Todos mis parientes vinieron a la boda.
example_en: All my relatives came to the wedding.

disambiguation_tip: You eat sopa with a spoon and wash your hands with jabón.
example_es: Pedimos una sopa caliente para la cena.
example_en: We ordered a hot soup for dinner.

disambiguation_tip: Usually means a binding commitment, social obligation, or engagement rather than meeting halfway.
example_es: No puedo ir porque tengo otro compromiso esta tarde.
example_en: I cannot go because I have another commitment this afternoon.

disambiguation_tip: Refers to upbringing and courtesy at home (polite); academic schooling is culto or con estudios.
example_es: El camarero fue muy amable y educado con nosotros.
example_en: The waiter was very kind and polite with us.

disambiguation_tip: An everyday, mild word meaning to bother or disturb ('Perdón por molestar' = 'Sorry to bother you').
example_es: Disculpa, ¿te molesta si abro la ventana?
example_en: Excuse me, does it bother you if I open the window?

disambiguation_tip: In everyday Spanish, discutir carries much more heat (arguing or clashing) than a neutral English 'discussion'.
example_es: Los vecinos discutieron durante horas por el ruido.
example_en: The neighbors argued for hours over the noise.

actual_english: to insert / put in / bring in
disambiguation_tip: You introducir a key into a lock or a password into a form, but you presentar a friend to another person.
example_es: Introduzca su contraseña para continuar.
example_en: Enter your password to continue.
